source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Uncomplicated concussion, because rapid deterioration after a lucid interval is expected and benign","B":"Chronic subdural hematoma, which always produces the same brief lucid interval after a head injury","C":"Epidural hematoma, often involving traumatic injury to the middle meningeal artery after skull trauma","D":"Ischemic stroke, because a traumatic lucid interval specifically indicates cerebral arterial embolism"}}
source_row.rationale: A lucid interval after traumatic loss of consciousness followed by neurologic deterioration is classically associated with epidural hematoma, often from middle meningeal arterial injury. The pattern is not present in every epidural hematoma and is not pathognomonic.
source_row.source_detail: History and Physical: classic lucid interval; etiology commonly middle meningeal artery after blunt trauma; last update July 7, 2025; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: After head trauma, a client briefly loses consciousness, becomes alert, then rapidly deteriorates neurologically. Which injury is classically associated with this lucid-interval pattern?
